clue.text: Awful din in brazen parade

indicators.note: in tells us the jumbled din goes inside the word for brazen

parts.note: brazen means brash, shamelessly bold

indicators.note: awful suggests something botched, so the letters of din are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a dreadful racket at a shameless procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parade' is a verb here, as in parading one's wealth, not a procession; 'Awful' scrambles DIN to NDI before 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to show it off, and to wave a sword or flag about boastfully is the same flourish.

clue.text: Horse battalion initially right to take on small company

indicators.note: initially means we take only the opening letter of battalion

parts.note: taken as written
CO is the short form of company, so a small company

explanation.surface: A military unit, first on the right, is to recruit a small firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild or half-tamed horse of the American West, the kind ridden at rodeos.

clue.text: Honeysuckle I label incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly means the letters of I label are set down in the wrong order

parts.note: the setter's fodder is these two words, but as printed they hold an L where a second A is needed, so the letters meant are one L short and one A over

explanation.surface: A gardener admits putting the wrong tag on a honeysuckle plant.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'incorrectly' rearranges I LABEL, which has an L where ABELIA needs a second A: a setter's slip of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abelia is a flowering shrub in the honeysuckle family, so the family name stands for one of its members.

clue.text: Passed over, crossing river — then fell off!

indicators.note: crossing means the word for died goes across, around the letter for river

parts.note: passed over is a euphemism for died, so deceased

explanation.surface: Someone died while fording a river, having fallen off a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed over' looks like a journey across the river, but it is the euphemism for dying; 'crossing' then puts R inside DECEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales or numbers that fell off went down, which is to say they diminished.

clue.text: Less valuable gems — bad copies I'm sure

indicators.note: bad copies hints at faulty reproduction, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller dismisses some stones as poor fakes with confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Stones such as amethyst or garnet rank below diamonds and rubies in worth, a lower grade of jewel.

clue.text: Stand for party on returning from expedition

parts.note: a trip is an expedition or outing

indicators.note: returning means the word for party is read backwards, placed on the end

parts.note: do is a common informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone on the way back from a trip wants a stand for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is positional: the turned party goes on, that is after, the trip. The grid printed TRIROD, not a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera or telescope is a kind of stand.

clue.text: River heron make for?

indicators.note: make for, with its question mark, hints that the letters of heron can be made into something else

explanation.surface: A heron heads for the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'make for' as heading somewhere; it actually says the letters of HERON can make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Figure dog is following the writer

indicators.note: is following means the word for dog comes after the word for the writer

parts.note: a pen is the thing that does the writing
to dog someone is to tag on behind them, following closely

explanation.surface: A drawing shows a dog trailing after an author.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints RENTAGON; PEN plus TAG ON builds PENTAGON, the five-sided figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a geometric shape with five sides, a plane figure in the mathematical sense.

clue.text: Analyse change in dosage

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in in dosage

explanation.surface: A doctor is asked to assess an adjustment to a patient's medication.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify an illness by examining symptoms is to analyse a case.

clue.text: Defeated, though played move with care

indicators.note: played suggests a move in a game being made, so the letters of move and care are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone won despite making a cautious move in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two fodder words MOVE and CARE and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or conquer an opponent or difficulty is to have defeated it.

clue.text: Set off with girl to see large lizard

parts.note: to set off is to go
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man heads out with a young woman to look at a big reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: A goanna is an Australian monitor lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: The goanna is a monitor, a big Australian reptile of the lizard family.

clue.text: Sleep centres around having no deceit

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of sleep centres are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleep clinic is described as an honest place.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of sham or affectation, a person who never puts on an act is without deceit.

clue.text: Boy caught and charged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a charged wire is live, carrying current

explanation.surface: A lad is arrested and charged by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' reads as a criminal charge, but it means electrically live.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive is a man's name, and crosswords use boy for any male first name.

clue.text: No replica possible for such fine china

indicators.note: possible hints that another arrangement of the letters of no replica can be made

explanation.surface: An antique dealer says this delicate china cannot be copied.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is the translucent ceramic used for the finest tableware.

clue.text: Tattoos in use, out of place and vulgar

indicators.note: out of place means the letters of tattoos in use are put in other positions

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that displayed tattoos are inappropriate and tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy display meant to impress is regarded as tasteless and vulgar.

clue.text: Type of plane needed for tour bopper organised, out east

indicators.note: organised means the remaining letters are arranged into a new order
out means the letter for east is removed from tour bopper

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A dancer touring needs a particular aircraft arranged, heading out east.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E from TOUR BOPPER to leave TOURBOPPR, then 'organised' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft driven by propellers turned by a gas turbine is a kind of plane.

clue.text: Wandering woolly bear right ahead of social worker

indicators.note: ahead of means the letter for right comes before the social worker
woolly suggests something fuzzy or muddled, so the letters of bear are mixed

parts.note: the ant is the classic social insect, and worker ants do the labour

explanation.surface: A shaggy bear wanders past a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' turns BEAR into ABER. A 'social worker' is not a case officer but an ant, the social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant behaviour strays from the normal path, so it is wandering off course.

clue.text: Study fair and make further amendment

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
fair means just, equitable

explanation.surface: Someone reviews a document carefully and makes another change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' meaning READ is the British university sense: one reads history.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter or set something again is to amend it once more.

clue.text: Successful racing stables heard to have done this for wage-earners

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is spoken, giving a sound like the answer

parts.note: stables that are successful have bred winners, horses that win races

explanation.surface: Thriving racing yards are said to have produced the family's earners.
explanation.walkthrough: Racing stables that succeed have bred winners; said aloud, that phrase is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of a household whose earnings support it are those who bring home the pay.

clue.text: Cooking they need half the gas

indicators.note: cooking suggests ingredients being worked over, so the letters of they are mixed
half means we take just the first part of need

explanation.surface: Chefs need only half the gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' scrambles THEY into ETHY; 'half' takes NE from NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyne, also called acetylene, is a flammable hydrocarbon used in welding torches.

clue.text: Growth leading cattle to get sick in south Africa

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the letters for south and Africa

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
A is a short form for Africa

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of cattle

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: A herd's leader falls ill in the south of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south Africa' looks like the place but gives S and A, which surround C and ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Scilla, or squill, is a bulb plant with blue flowers; a plant is a growth.

clue.text: Game bird flushed? Complain!

parts.note: someone flushed has gone red in the face
to grouse is to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: A shooter asks whether the game bird has been flushed out, and grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flushed' suggests driving birds from cover, but it means red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse is a moorland game species shot in Britain from the Glorious Twelfth.

clue.text: A proportion of the operation

indicators.note: of the says part of the following word supplies the letters, a run inside operation

explanation.surface: Something is part of the procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a quantitative relationship between two amounts, such as three to one.

clue.text: Bar measure a tricky topic?

indicators.note: tricky suggests the topic is awkward, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Measures served in a pub turn out to be a difficult subject.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is the device fixed to an upside-down bottle in a British bar that dispenses a fixed measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pub spirits are poured through a gadget that releases a set amount, a measure at the bar.

clue.text: Showing ingenuity found centre in metropolis

indicators.note: in means that middle letter goes inside the letters for the metropolis

parts.note: a metropolis is a big city; the setter lets the single word stand for 'a city', article and all

indicators.note: centre means only the middle letter of the word found is used

explanation.surface: Someone proves clever by finding the heart of a great city.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: 'Showing' is only a link, and 'metropolis' has to give A CITY although no 'a' is printed; 'centre' takes U from FOUND, which 'in' puts after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is sharpness of mind or perception, close to cleverness or ingenuity.

clue.text: Breaking of trust by three small boys

parts.note: Bet is offered as a short name; it is really a pet form of Elizabeth, a girl's name, but the setter counts it among the boys
Ray is a short form of Raymond
Al is a short form of Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: Trust is broken by a trio of little lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small boys' means short forms of names, not children. Ray and Al are fine, but Bet is normally short for Elizabeth, so the setter has slipped there.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is the act of being disloyal and violating someone's confidence.

clue.text: Indelible impression made by drumming

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is permanent ink marking on skin; the other is a rhythmic beating, as on a drum or a military evening display.

clue.text: Raise pot, shake! Termites may emerge!

indicators.note: shake means the letters of raise pot are tossed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lift a pot and shake it, and insects may crawl out.
explanation.definitionFit: Isoptera is the zoological order name for these wood-eating insects.
